- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast, especially in the first 10–15 days of the 30d horizon — reduce early peaks.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30), model under-responds to downward momentum — increase early declines or add downward bias to first 5–7 days.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +0.50+ sentiment) — cap forecast peaks at 1–2 days after spike, then allow gradual decay.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted — model tends to hold high prices longer than observed; apply a 3–5 day decay factor to forecasted highs.
- Forecast horizon 1–5 days: model is overly optimistic; reduce by 0.5–1.5% per day relative to recent 7-day average.
- Forecast horizon 6–15 days: model often misses downward correction — add 0.5–1.0% downward bias if sentiment turns negative.
- Forecast horizon 16–30 days: model tends to overestimate late-term volatility — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 14-day high if sentiment is neutral or negative.
